notes.meaning: David calls out to God in deep trouble and asks Him not to discipline him in burning anger. He admits that he deserves correction, but he asks for fatherly mercy rather than harsh punishment. The heading mentions stringed instruments and an eighth key or eight-stringed instrument.

David pleads for God to show mercy because his strength is completely gone. His illness and sorrow have shaken him to his very bones, which means his entire body and inner being are in pain. He knows no earthly doctor can cure him, so he asks God to heal him.

David is deeply terrified and troubled in his soul under the weight of God's discipline. He asks God how long this severe trial must go on before relief comes. His sentence breaks off suddenly because his grief is too heavy for full words.

David asks the Lord to turn back toward him and rescue his life. It feels to him as if God has stepped away and hidden His face. David does not claim any good deeds of his own, but pleads for rescue purely based on God's faithful mercy.

David points out that the dead cannot speak to others of God's goodness from the grave. In the Old Testament, the realm of the dead is called Sheol, where people no longer join the congregation in public praise. David asks to be spared so he can keep honoring God and telling others of His grace in this life.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars say the psalm writers pictured only one shadowy place for all the dead, far from God's light. In this view, Christians pray this verse by thinking of hell, where there truly is no praise of God.

notes.meaning: David is worn out from groaning through long, sleepless nights. He uses vivid language to say his tears drench his bed until it seems to swim. Even a brave ruler can weep deeply when humbled by sin and the pain of God's correction.

David's eyes have grown weak and blurry from shedding so many tears. His face looks aged and worn down because of his continuous grief and the cruelty of his foes. Dim eyes show that a person's physical strength is rapidly fading away.

David suddenly commands all evil people to leave him alone. His sorrow turns into boldness because he knows God has listened to his weeping. The Lord treats quiet tears as a real, powerful cry for help.

David repeats with full assurance that the Lord has heard his plea for mercy. He is certain that God welcomes his prayer and will not reject it. God has placed peace in his heart even before the outward trouble has fully vanished.

David is confident that all his enemies will be thrown into sudden shame and confusion. Their wicked schemes will fail completely when God steps in to deliver His servant. Their unexpected disappointment will show everyone that God defends the afflicted.
